qa_pairs.question: How can researchers use the SHARCNET Ansys license for AnsysEDT modules on Alliance clusters?
qa_pairs.answer: Researchers can use the SHARCNET Ansys license for AnsysEDT modules on any Alliance cluster for free. This is achieved by configuring their `~/.licenses/ansys.lic` file to include the following lines: `setenv("ANSYSLMD_LICENSE_FILE", "1055@license3.sharcnet.ca")` and `setenv("ANSYSLI_SERVERS", "2325@license3.sharcnet.ca")`.

qa_pairs.question: What are the steps to retrieve and run the 2024R2.1 Antennas examples in AnsysEDT?
qa_pairs.answer: To retrieve the 2024R2.1 Antennas examples, first load the module with `module load ansysedt/2024R2.1`. Then, copy the examples to your account using `mkdir -p ~/Ansoft/$EBVERSIONANSYSEDT; rm -rf ~/Ansoft/$EBVERSIONANSYSEDT/Antennas` followed by `cp -a $EBROOTANSYSEDT/v242/Linux64/Examples/HFSS/Antennas ~/Ansoft/$EBVERSIONANSYSEDT`. To run an example, open one of the `.aedt` files, click `HFSS -> Validation Check`, then navigate `Simulation -> setup -> advanced -> Mesh/Solution options -> Use Defaults`, and finally `Simulation -> Analyze All`. To quit without saving, select `File -> Close -> No`.

qa_pairs.question: What steps should be taken if AnsysEDT crashes and fails to restart?
qa_pairs.answer: If AnsysEDT crashes and won't restart, you should run two commands: `pkill -9 -u $USER -f "ansys*|mono|mwrpcss|apip-standalone-service"` to terminate related processes, and `rm -rf ~/.mw` to remove old configuration files, which will prompt AnsysEDT to re-run its first-time setup upon the next launch.
